subtype: Stage 1: The bully picks a target [Actor]
passage: Mohit, you asked why I'm so strict about teasing. Let your Sudha Nani tell you something I've never told your mother. When I was nine, my father shouted every evening. At home I was small, invisible. At school I wanted to be big. There was a girl in my class, Kusum, very quiet, who ate alone and never answered back. I noticed her the way a cat notices a sparrow. She had done nothing to me. Nothing at all. But the other girls laughed when I teased her, and for once people looked at me like I mattered. That's what I wanted, beta. Not to hurt her exactly. To feel strong. It took me many years to understand that.

qa.q: What was the quiet girl's name in Sudha Nani's class?
What did Sudha Nani really want when she chose Kusum?
qa.a: She wanted to feel strong and noticed, because at home she felt small and invisible with her father shouting.

qa.q: If an adult had noticed nine-year-old Sudha at this first stage, what could they have done?
qa.a: They could have given her real ways to feel important, like responsibility in class, and paid attention to what was going on at home, while protecting Kusum.

qa.q: How might Kusum have experienced being picked out?
qa.a: She probably felt confused and scared, since she had done nothing and couldn't understand why she was chosen.

grounding: It shows a child who felt powerless at home choosing a quiet classmate as a target to gain status, not because of anything the classmate did.

subtype: Stage 1: The bully picks a target [Actor]
passage: Rain hammered the tin roof and recess was cancelled, so class 4B stayed inside while their teacher was called away. Uday leaned back on his bench. At home, his two older brothers took the TV remote, the bigger roti, the last word. Here he wanted to be the one people watched. His eyes moved around the room. Tanmay would shove back. Rupa's friends would tell. Then he saw Harsha, drawing quietly in the corner, alone, shoulders curled. Harsha never argued, even when someone took his crayons. Uday smiled a little. He glanced at the boys near him to make sure they were watching, then stood up and strolled over, slowly, the whole class suddenly quiet.

qa.q: What took away recess for class 4B?
qa.a: The rain hammered the tin roof and recess was cancelled.

qa.q: Why might Uday want to be watched at school?
qa.a: At home his older brothers take everything and he feels small and powerless, so he wants to feel important in front of the class.

qa.q: What could a teacher do at this stage, before anything happens?
qa.a: Not leave the class unsupervised for long, notice Uday's need for status, and give him a positive role, while keeping an eye on quieter children like Harsha.

qa.q: How might Harsha feel as Uday walks over?
qa.a: Harsha may feel nervous and confused, not knowing what he did, when in fact he did nothing at all.

grounding: It illustrates a child who feels powerless at home looking for status and choosing a quiet classmate who does not fight back.
